literature_notes: The entire ledger (L1, L2) describes zebrafish clrn1 (Clarin-1) carrying a C-terminal HA tag. Zebrafish clrn1 is the species ortholog of human CLRN1, not CLRN3; CLRN1 and CLRN3 are paralogs (distinct genes in the clarin family) and the ledger rule requires the same gene in a close ortholog, not a paralog. Even setting aside the ortholog issue, the C-terminal tag in L1/L2 would map to CLRN3 residues 201–226, which the authoritative topology landmarks place entirely intracellular (INTRACELLULAR: 201–226). No ledger line reports any insertion — epitope tag, fluorescent-protein fusion, transposon, or domain-insertion — in either of CLRN3's two extracellular loops (EC1: 29–93; EC2: 148–179) or at any extracellular position of this protein or a true ortholog. Zero surface tag sites qualify.
